articles.title: Technicals signal bitcoin shift, Ethereum gears up for Glamsterdam: Crypto Week Ahead
articles.description: Your look at what's coming in the week starting Oct. 5.

articles.title: Kraken operator Payward and Singapore Gulf Bank platform for 24/7 institutional crypto settlement
articles.description: The two firms will initially roll out the digital assets settlement service to select institutional clients in Asia and the Gulf region with around-the-clock U.S. dollar settlement.

articles.title: Bitcoin is about to get a major bullish signal it hasn't had in over a year
articles.description: Key price averages are on the verge of confirming a major bullish configuration for the first time in over a year.

articles.title: Ethereum investors are stuck in a two-week staking exit line. Here's why.
articles.description: Ether waiting to enter staking has fallen by more than a quarter since early September, while the exit queue hit its longest of 2026.

articles.title: Joint venture of OKX and NYSE parent ICE files for 24/7 tokenized U.S. stock trading
articles.description: OKXICE, the joint venture of OKX and ICE, plans to launch tokenized U.S. stocks under SEC's new innovation exemption.

articles.title: Zcash’s 25-second blocks go live on public testnet ahead of schedule
articles.description: NU7 cuts the target block time from 75 seconds to 25, giving exchanges, wallets and developers a live rehearsal before a planned November mainnet launch.

articles.title: Bitcoin zooms toward $87,000, nearly setting an eight-month high, then reverses
articles.description: Bitcoin came within about $500 of its late-September peak before sellers pushed it back under $86,000. It's the second rally in a week to stall.

articles.title: Ether's bitcoin-beating Q3 rally came with a catch. Liquidity thinned.
articles.description: Ether beat bitcoin in the third quarter, but its market liquidity got thinner, according to Coingecko.

articles.title: There's an election next month: State of Crypto
articles.description: Congress is gone from Washington for the final pre-election recess, and it's time to take stock of what's going on ahead of November.

articles.title: Crypto poured years into new products. The next challenge is keeping users
articles.description: Crypto firms have spent years building financial products on blockchains. Getting people to use them — and keep using them — is becoming the next challenge.

articles.title: The Clarity Act stalled. Bankers aren’t hitting the brakes yet on crypto dealmaking
articles.description: Crypto M&A has hit record levels, but the Clarity Act’s Senate setback leaves dealmakers weighing how much regulatory uncertainty still matters.

articles.title: Payments firm OpenPayd targets year-end Nasdaq listing to fund U.S. expansion and acquisitions
articles.description: CEO Iana Dimitrova said OpenPayd aims to launch in the U.S. by April 2027 and is eyeing deals to add licenses and technology.

articles.title: Crypto job postings triple to over 1,200 in September, but applications fall
articles.description: Finance, engineering and trading led hiring demand, while Bitcoin, Ethereum and Solana were the most frequently requested blockchain skills.

articles.title: Cathie Wood says smart investors need to start watching where AI agents spend money
articles.description: As AI agents evolve from answering questions to spending real money, investors and tech giants are scrambling to control the financial networks powering machine-driven commerce.

articles.title: Crypto's Sisyphean struggle
articles.description: Progress will effectively reset when the new Congress is sworn in, because key senators who quarterbacked the bill will not be on the ballot again, writes the Cato Institute's Ryan Chan-Wei.

articles.title: BlackRock offers a glimpse of how tokenization may change your investment portfolio
articles.description: Tokenization is not just about putting individual stocks and funds onchain. The next step could be entire investment portfolios that can be traded, rebalanced and eventually managed in real-time.

articles.title: Bank group sues U.S. regulator over granting crypto trust charters
articles.description: The Independent Community Bankers of America sued the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, accusing the regulator of overstepping its legal authority.

articles.title: BNY in talks with Kraken parent Payward over infrastructure partnership
articles.description: The potential agreement could span digital assets, custody, trading, payments and other financial-market infrastructure.

articles.title: Once a $2 billion Ethereum layer-2, Blast is shutting down after assets plunge 98%
articles.description: Once home to more than $2 billion in crypto assets, Blast is shutting down as activity fades, costs rise, and bigger platforms like Coinbase and Robinhood build networks of their own.

articles.title: Trump’s potential AI czar, Jay Clayton, helped pioneer the SEC’s crypto crackdown
articles.description: The former SEC chairman who may be tapped to oversee the Trump administration's AI work has a potentially divisive history as a watchdog of tech innovation.

articles.title: America at a crossroads: Commissioner Peirce’s parting challenge
articles.description: It is incumbent upon us to continue Commissioner Peirce’s mission, writes Will Schwartz, policy associate at the Blockchain Association.

articles.title: U.S. added just 29,000 jobs in September, with unemployment rate rising to 4.2%
articles.description: Bitcoin held earlier gains following the report, up more than 2% over the past 24 hours and just below $87,000.

articles.title: Crypto traders are in risk-on mode as bitcoin dominance nears return to 60%
articles.description: Bitcoin dominance is closing in on 60% while USDT's has slipped to 6.3%, pointing to a market growing more comfortable with risk.
